source_name: Erste Group Procurement – Code of Conduct (EGP supplier rulebook PDF)
why_relevant: The named rulebook that gates EGP's standardised supplier onboarding, and therefore gates any vendor wanting to sell into Česká spořitelna. Concrete, citable onboarding precondition rather than a general CSR statement.

source_name: Raiffeisenbank a.s. (CZ) – Code of Conduct for Suppliers / Etický kodex dodavatelů
source_subtype: bank supplier code of conduct page
why_relevant: The Czech Raiffeisenbank entity's own supplier-facing page, published under a Czech-language slug (eticky-kodex-dodavatelu) with an EN rendering. Sets out seven binding principles for RBI suppliers: EU sanctions/embargo screening, UN climate and ILO alignment, social responsibility, environmental responsibility, business integrity (anti-corruption, competition law, AML/CFT), flow-down to sub-contractors, and RBI's audit and reporting rights. Confirms RBI's audit right over suppliers — materially relevant to any vendor pricing an RB CZ engagement. Also carries the RBI whistleblower channel (rbi.whispli.com/whistleblowing).

source_name: RBI Group – Code of Conduct / responsible banking (Raiffeisenbank CZ parent)
why_relevant: The group source from which the CZ supplier code derives; the CZ page states the code applies to all RBI business units and subsidiaries. Watching the group page catches supplier-requirement changes before they surface on rb.cz. RBI network sister pages (e.g. rba.hr, raiffeisenbank.ba) republish the same instrument, giving cross-checks on the current version.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank – Procurement principles page (RBI network, UA instance)
source_subtype: peer-subsidiary procurement page used as template proxy
why_relevant: Raiffeisenbank CZ publishes no procurement-process page, but a sister RBI subsidiary does — 'transparency and partnership, principles of procurement activity'. As a proxy it shows the RBI house template for how a network bank runs supplier selection and e-auctions, letting an analyst infer the RB CZ process shape and the right questions to ask. Explicitly a proxy, not evidence about CZ.

source_name: MONETA Money Bank – Etický kodex dodavatele (Supplier Code of Ethics)
source_subtype: supplier code of ethics PDF (filed under general documents)
why_relevant: MONETA has no 'for suppliers' section; its only public supplier instrument is the Etický kodex dodavatele PDF, filed among general downloadable documents (path /documents/20143/11740692/mmb-eticky-kodex-dodavatele-cz.pdf) and mirrored in English on the MONETA ESG site. Its placement among ordinary documents rather than a supplier hub is itself the finding — MONETA's sourcing is entirely non-public and bilateral.

source_name: MONETA ESG document library
why_relevant: Separate MONETA subdomain carrying the EN Code of Ethics for Suppliers plus the group anti-corruption policy. ESG/CSRD reporting is becoming the main place Czech banks disclose anything quantitative about their supply chain (supplier counts, screening rates, local-spend shares), so this library is the likeliest future home of supplier-base statistics.

source_name: wflow.com – Česká spořitelna purchasing-automation customer page
why_relevant: A Czech procure-to-pay vendor publishing a Česká spořitelna-branded page about automating company purchasing/invoice workflow. Two uses: it evidences the P2P tooling layer around ČS, and it shows ČS acting as a channel partner pushing procurement software to its SME clients — relevant to understanding where ČS's own vendor stack sits. Vendor marketing, so treat claims as directional and verify the exact nature of the relationship before relying on it.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Udržitelnost hub and Sustainability Report (in Annual Report 2024)
why_relevant: With no ČS supplier portal, the sustainability/annual-report track is the bank's only first-party channel that discusses its supply chain. ČS states minimum ethical standards are set at Erste Group level and that it addresses sustainability at the level of clients AND suppliers; the Sustainability Report is embedded in the 2024 Annual Report. Under CSRD this is where any quantitative supplier-base disclosure will appear.

source_name: ČSOB Pojišťovna – Informační memorandum pro dodavatele (GDPR notice for suppliers)
why_relevant: Supplier-facing privacy memorandum from a ČSOB group company. Reveals-indirectly source: to explain what personal data it processes, it enumerates the artefacts of the group's procurement process — supplier records, contracts, orders, invoices, shopping-cart/purchase-order tracking. That is a free description of the ČSOB group P2P data model, obtainable nowhere else publicly. A parallel document exists for ČSOB Penzijní/PM entities.

source_name: MPO – Pravidla pro výběr dodavatelů (rules for supplier selection outside ZZVZ)
why_relevant: Ministry of Industry and Trade rulebook for supplier selection by non-ZZVZ entities. Matters to this cell as the legal boundary condition: it explains when a private body such as a bank IS pulled into formalised, publishable tendering — chiefly when the purchase is co-funded by EU/state subsidy. Any CZ bank running a subsidised project therefore becomes visible in the public tender record. This is the main pathway by which an otherwise invisible private-bank purchase surfaces.

source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách – zadávací vs. poptávkové (výběrové) řízení guidance
why_relevant: Official MMR-run public-procurement portal Q&A distinguishing zadávací řízení (under the ZZVZ public procurement act) from poptávkové/výběrové řízení (outside it), including publication duties. This is the terminology backbone for the whole cell: private banks run poptávkové řízení, which carries NO publication duty — the structural reason this cell has almost no notice-level sources. Essential for building correct Czech query vocabulary and for not mistaking absence of notices for absence of activity.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf – ČSOB case study (ATM network outsourcing, DN Series cash recycling)
why_relevant: Named customer reference documenting a private-sector CZ award: entire ČSOB ATM fleet supplied, maintained and operated end-to-end by Diebold Nixdorf, ~200 DN Series recyclers, 20-year relationship, uptime/CIT metrics. This is exactly the vendor-side trace of a bank deal that never appears in any public tender register.

source_name: PR Newswire – 'CSOB Partners with Diebold Nixdorf to Achieve its Vision of Tellerless Branches'
why_relevant: Wire-distributed vendor win announcement naming a Czech bank and the scope (tellerless branch transformation). Wire syndication mirrors survive even when the vendor later removes the release from its own newsroom — useful as an archival redundancy path.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe – Reference (CZ) page
why_relevant: Vendor-maintained customer list naming Czech banks and building societies (Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, MONETA, ČSOB stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida per search summary). A logo/reference page is the cheapest longitudinal signal of who won which core-banking / building-society estate.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe – Press room / annual reports (CZ)
why_relevant: Asseco CE is listed on the Warsaw exchange via Asseco Poland; its CZ press room and annual reports disclose contract wins and segment revenue by customer type — a semi-regulated confirmation channel for deals that press releases only hint at.

source_name: Cleverlance – Novinky (news): 'Jak Cleverlance přispívá k růstu Banky Creditas'
why_relevant: Czech systems integrator publishing a named bank engagement (Banka CREDITAS). Integrator news pages are often the only public trace of mid-size CZ bank IT awards, which are entirely outside public procurement.

source_name: Enehano Solutions – Případové studie (Česká spořitelna)
why_relevant: Smaller CZ implementation partner publishing a named Česká spořitelna case study. Small vendors disclose more scope detail than large ones because each logo matters more to them — high information density per reference.

source_name: LLP CRM – case study: CRM implementation at Raiffeisenbank (CZ)
why_relevant: Named Raiffeisenbank CZ implementation reference, and it snowballs to Trask as methodology/integration-layer partner — a pointer to a second vendor on the same account.

source_name: KB SmartPay – 'Komerční banka a Worldline rozšíří možnosti plateb kartami v ČR'
why_relevant: Joint-venture/alliance announcement between Komerční banka and Worldline covering merchant acquiring and payment terminals in CZ — a private-sector award of the largest possible kind, announced only on the vendor/JV side.

source_name: Worldline Česká republika – country site / newsroom
why_relevant: Worldline's CZ country site is the local-language publication point for CZ acquiring, terminal-estate and bank-partnership announcements (KB SmartPay and beyond).

source_name: Časopis Bankovnictví (bankovnictvionline.cz) – vendor/bank announcement republication
why_relevant: Czech banking trade magazine that republishes bank-and-vendor announcements (e.g. Česká spořitelna + Global Payments terminal offer). Acts as an aggregator that catches vendor claims which never get an English release, and provides dated, citable versions.

source_name: Verifone – partner taxonomy page for Printec Czech Republic, s.r.o.
why_relevant: Vendor partner/distributor directories reveal the supply chain behind CZ POS estates: who is authorised to deploy which terminal brand. Printec CZ appearing as a Verifone partner is an indirect indicator of which acquirer estates it can serve.

source_name: Printec Group – corporate site and country pages (CZ/SK)
why_relevant: Integrator of exactly the profile this cell targets (self-service channels, cash handling, payment platforms across CEE). Its country pages, news and any case-study section are the primary trace of CZ bank/retail deployments it wins.

source_name: NCR Atleos – corporate site / newsroom
why_relevant: Primary publication point for NCR Atleos ATM-as-a-Service, cash-recycling and network deals. CZ is named in at least one multi-country contactless-ATM announcement, so CZ-specific detail plausibly sits in this newsroom or in wire releases.

source_name: Mastercard newsroom – 'Mastercard, NCR Atleos, and ITCARD to enhance contactless experiences at ATMs' (CZ named)
why_relevant: Scheme-side release naming Czech Republic among markets with deployed contactless ATMs. Card schemes announce capability rollouts that implicitly identify which vendor/processor estates were upgraded — a back door into private deployments.

source_name: ATM Marketplace – vendor news & media hubs (NCR Atleos, Auriga, Diebold)
why_relevant: Trade aggregator that indexes vendor announcements and product showcases by company, making it an efficient single crawl point to discover new self-service vendor claims that may name CZ banks.
